tool.title: Replay a committed mount lock with nothing but Node
tool.description: Lay down every remote mount `index.lock.json` records — each layer fetched at the lock's full SHA (sparse, blob-filtered), each directory verified against its `treeDigest`, a mismatch undone and reported — importing only `node:*`, so it runs on a fresh clone before any layer is present. It never decides what to mount: `remote-mount` writes the lock (and checks trust); this only replays it. Refuses to write over a path with tracked files or bytes that no longer hash to the lock. Exit 0 mounted/current, 1 missing, 2 could-not-determine.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: The layer root whose lock is replayed. Default: the working directory.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: No network: is every locked mount on disk and intact?

outputs.name: outcomes
outputs.description: Per layer: mounted, current, missing or could-not-determine.

selection.when: First step of a CI job or session on a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount, after the lock is committed.
selection.limits: It lives in cat-harness, which is itself a mounted layer, so it cannot bootstrap a checkout that does not already hold cat-harness. The parent must carry its own dependency-free entry point that fetches this script at the pin (e.g. a `.github/mount-from-lock.sh`) — never call this path directly from a workflow in a repository that mounts cat-harness. A downstream root's `cat` script, `bun .github/cat.ts`, runs that entry point when the layers are missing, so `bun run cat <name>` works from `git clone`.
selection.cost: One shallow, blob-filtered fetch per locked layer; a few seconds each. `--check` needs no network.

remedies.none: Replaying a lock IS fetching the pinned repositories; offline, `--check` still reports what is on disk.

$comment.comment:
`mount-from-lock.ts` had no Tool node, so the one step every CI job and
every folio's staging build runs FIRST was invisible to an agent looking
for tooling — and when the cat-harness cutover (2026-10-09) took it out
of the parent's tree, every job failed at that step with nothing to say
what the step was (skill `kg-separation`, lessons 16–17).
